findings.concise_factual_summary: GitLab remediated two MCP authorization and data-boundary flaws: one race in MCP search shared-state handling could return search results under the wrong user context, and one improper authorization check could let an authenticated MCP-scoped token perform actions outside its intended scope.
findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability records plus vendor release reference
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: GitLab CE/EE: CVE-2026-92628 affects 18.6 before 19.2.7, 19.3 before 19.3.3, and 19.4 before 19.4.1; CVE-2026-92874 affects 18.3 before 19.2.7, 19.3 before 19.3.3, and 19.4 before 19.4.1.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: GitLab's MCP layer mediates agent access to repository search and actions; the records show why scoped MCP tokens and per-user tool state must be isolated at execution time, not only at token issuance.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: identity-and-access and agent-and-tool-security should own the MCP token-scope and search-result isolation analysis.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Broad GitLab product and MCP ecosystem context belongs upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent repository workflow implications belong upstream if not framed as a security control.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from direct CVE Services data and GitLab release reference; vendor work item links may require GitLab access or change visibility.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, decide whether these remain one GitLab MCP control-plane leaf or split into search isolation and scoped-token authorization leaves.
Verify the GitLab patch release page exposes both CVEs and fixed versions before durable synthesis.

findings.concise_factual_summary: Five CVEs describe mcp-remote OAuth and transport flaws, including SSRF through OAuth metadata URLs, sensitive information exposure through authorization-server metadata and SSE token-origin handling, and code-execution paths tied to server URL hashing or browser URL validation.
findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE records plus public research/advisory repository references
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: mcp-remote is a client-side bridge that brokers remote MCP server authorization; metadata, token, URL, and browser-open handling bugs can turn server discovery and delegated authorization into SSRF, token exposure, or code execution boundaries.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: agent-and-tool-security and identity-and-access own OAuth metadata, token-origin, SSRF, and code-execution boundaries for MCP client bridges.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Broad mcp-remote package background belongs upstream if the entity is cataloged.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General MCP client troubleshooting or developer setup belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence that records are in-window and AI-security relevant; affected arrays in CVE Services are sparse, so ingest should verify patched release information from GitHub advisories or commits.
follow_up_actions: Fetch the referenced GitHub Security Advisories during ingest to identify patched versions and remediation text.
Consider one cluster leaf because all five records share the same client bridge and OAuth/remote-server trust boundary.

findings.concise_factual_summary: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway exposed a path traversal in its Admin API log-download endpoint because path confinement used string-prefix comparison instead of boundary-aware validation, allowing an authenticated admin to read certain log-like files outside the configured log directory.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP gateways often centralize agent traffic, tool calls, and audit logs; path traversal in log retrieval can expose model/tool traces, request metadata, or secrets accidentally written to logs.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: agent-and-tool-security owns gateway log-access boundaries and path traversal analysis.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: General IBM ContextForge entity context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General MCP gateway deployment practice belongs upstream unless framed as a security control.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from IBM PSIRT-sourced CVE record; IBM support page should be refetched during ingest for fixed version and workaround wording.
follow_up_actions: Verify whether IBM lists a fixed ContextForge MCP Gateway release after 1.0.8.
During synthesis, connect to local MCP gateway logging and audit-evidence pages if present.

findings.concise_factual_summary: DBHub had two MCP database-boundary flaws: HTTP transport before 0.22.5 could be reached through DNS rebinding despite Origin/Host checks, and read-only mode before 0.22.6 failed to make the database connection read-only, leaving only SQL keyword classification as enforcement.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: DBHub before 0.22.5 for HTTP transport DNS rebinding; DBHub before 0.22.6 for read-only enforcement failure.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Database MCP servers turn model or browser-mediated tool calls into database reads and writes; these records show that transport-origin checks and advertised read-only settings are security-critical enforcement points.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: agent-and-tool-security and data-and-privacy own DB MCP transport, read-only, and delegated database-access boundaries.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Broad DBHub entity page belongs upstream if cataloged.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General developer database-agent workflow belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from direct CVE Services and GitHub advisory URLs; GitHub advisory content should be read during ingest for exact patched release notes.
follow_up_actions: Synthesize as one DBHub MCP database-boundary leaf unless the read-only control needs a separate durable page.
Record that DNS rebinding is browser-origin exploitation without prompt injection or model involvement.

findings.concise_factual_summary: Decepticon before 1.1.17 composed web-crawl output into LLM messages without neutralizing ChatML special-token literals, allowing attacker content planted on a target page to forge a new operator turn for providers that parse those literals into role-boundary tokens.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The record is a concrete prompt/content-boundary vulnerability in an autonomous red-team agent, linking retrieved web content, model-provider tokenization behavior, and command execution inside a Kali sandbox.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: model-and-prompt-security and agent-and-tool-security own role-boundary forgery and autonomous-agent command-execution analysis.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Broad Decepticon and model-provider catalog context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General red-team-agent practice belongs upstream unless focused on security-control design.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from direct CVE Services data; ingest should verify exact remediation behavior from the GitHub advisory/commit.
follow_up_actions: Link to any existing prompt-injection or content-boundary pages during synthesis.

findings.concise_factual_summary: Amazon Kiro IDE before 1.0.242 could allow crafted instructions in an untrusted repository to cause agent modifications to auto-loaded global configuration paths, injecting content into the agent's future context.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Amazon Kiro IDE before 1.0.242 on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Coding agents often load global instructions across workspaces; this record makes the untrusted-repository to persistent-global-context boundary a concrete security control.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: agent-and-tool-security and data-and-privacy own persistent instruction/context modification and untrusted workspace boundaries.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Broad Amazon Kiro product context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent workspace practice belongs upstream; keep the vulnerability and mitigation boundary here.

findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The cluster is a concrete enterprise AI platform authorization, data-access, and SQL execution failure set, relevant to release gates for hosted and self-hosted AI control planes.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: identity-and-access, data-and-privacy, and governance/release-gates should own this AI Platform security cluster.

findings.concise_factual_summary: Discourse AI reviewables associated with private messages could appear in a moderator review queue for a moderator who was not a message participant, allowing private-message content exposure and possible edit/delete capability depending on reviewable actions.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI review queues can become a secondary access path to private user content; reviewable visibility must inherit the underlying conversation authorization boundary.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: data-and-privacy and identity-and-access own AI reviewable visibility and private-message authorization analysis.

findings.concise_factual_summary: MLflow's dspy flavor applies the MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=False control only when a model_path ends in .pkl, allowing remote code execution through a crafted MLmodel artifact.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MLflow dspy flavor versions >= 2.0 according to the CVE record.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model artifacts are executable supply-chain inputs; extension-based enforcement can fail when metadata or artifact formats route around the intended deserialization gate.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: infrastructure-and-supply-chain owns model artifact deserialization and runtime execution risk.

upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General MLOps/development workflow context belongs upstream.

findings.concise_factual_summary: TREK before 3.3.0 had two AI-tooling boundary flaws: its get_trip_summary MCP tool did not require trips:read for scoped OAuth tokens and returned trip metadata/member emails, and an authenticated user could set an attacker-controlled llm_base_url that the AI-assisted import path consumed, creating SSRF risk.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The records combine delegated MCP OAuth scope enforcement and user-configurable LLM endpoint trust, two recurring security boundaries for AI-enabled applications.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: identity-and-access, data-and-privacy, and agent-and-tool-security own the MCP scope and LLM endpoint SSRF analysis.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Broad TREK product context belongs upstream only if needed.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General app development use of LLM parsing belongs upstream.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from direct CVE Services; ingest should verify v3.3.0 release contents and GitHub advisories.
follow_up_actions: Decide whether to synthesize one TREK AI-tool boundary leaf or split OAuth scope and LLM-base-url SSRF.

findings.concise_factual_summary: OpenWA before 0.23.5 allowed a VIEWER-scoped API key to call the GroupGetInviteCode MCP tool and retrieve transferable WhatsApp group invite codes because the endpoint/tool lacked an OPERATOR role requirement.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP tools can expose bearer-like social or collaboration capabilities; role checks must map to the sensitivity of the external action or token returned.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: identity-and-access and agent-and-tool-security own MCP role-to-action mapping and transferable invite-code exposure.
